text:
Michael Kesselring has found a steady job in San Jose,. The 6-foot-5 defenseman from Florence, South Carolina, a sixth-round pick by Edmonton in 2018, came to the Sharks from Buffalo before last June's draft after stops in Arizona and Utah. He has played all 22 games, about 19 minutes a night, after only 34 games with the Sabres last season. Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest pointed to his skating again on Saturday, when it drew San Jose a power play against Utah.

The points have lagged the play. He has four assists and no goals on 30 shots, and his own chances add up to 1.67 expected goals (the quality of his shots), so a goal or two has gone missing. The bigger gap is around him: the Sharks have scored 6.1 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, the kind of shortfall that usually swings back. Their share of expected goals at five on five, 44% with him out there, is about what it is without him. He has been shooting more lately, 13 shots in his last four games, and that is the trend to watch.
headline: Michael Kesselring's steady minutes, missing goals
